# Story 104 — Reports: agent load with idle agents at zero (Story: CRM-128)

## Plan review — read this before the sections below

Reviewed 2026-09-02 against the code, every citation opened. The central
decision is right and stated well: the rows come from `users` with the counts
joined on, because a `GROUP BY tickets.assignee_id` cannot return the person
holding nothing and that person is who the report is for. **Seven things are
wrong.** Where a section below contradicts this one, this one wins.

### 1 — The census instruction, again. Do not touch that file.

Context item 8 tells the builder to put a case into the staff-only census, and
Test Plan step 2 tells them to put `GET /reports/agent-load` into its list of
"admin-only routes verified to 403". Neither should happen.

That file's only list is `OPEN_TO_A_CUSTOMER` — **routes a customer may
reach**, each with a written reason. Adding an admin-only route to it exempts
the route from the census rather than proving it. The census reads every route
off the mounted router; a new route is covered the moment it is mounted, and
mounting it with `adminOnly` is the whole of the work.

**This is the second consecutive plan to say it**, and `L-68` — written for the
first one — was already in `.squad/plan-lessons.md` when this plan was
generated, in the file the intake's standing block tells the planner to read
first. A hint that has failed twice in a row is not a mechanism. `verify-plan`
now fails a plan that tells the builder to edit a guarantee file, which is where
this belongs.

### 2 — `TERMINAL_STATUSES` is a derivation that is not one, and the word is wrong.

```js
const TERMINAL_STATUSES = STATUSES.filter((s) => s === 'resolved' || s === 'closed');
```

Both names are written into the filter. If `STATUSES` changed, nothing here
would follow — the set is not derived from anything, it is two literals passed
through a loop. That is **worse than writing the two literals plainly**, because
it claims a property it does not have and the next reader will believe it.

And "terminal" is wrong by this codebase's own definition.
`tickets.rules.js:196` has `resolved: ['closed', 'reopened']` and
`closed: Object.freeze([])` — `closed` is the only terminal status; a resolved
ticket has two moves left.

What this report means is **work still on the person**, and a resolved ticket is
off somebody's plate whether or not it can come back. That is a different idea
from terminality and it deserves its own name and its own sentence:

```js
// Off somebody's plate. NOT the same as terminal — TRANSITIONS (tickets.rules.js:194-201)
// says only `closed` is terminal, and a resolved ticket still has two moves.
// This is a statement about workload, not about the state machine, so it is
// written out rather than filtered out of STATUSES: there is nothing in
// STATUSES to derive it from, and a filter that names both members is two
// literals wearing a derivation.
const OFF_THE_PLATE = Object.freeze(['resolved', 'closed']);
```

### 3 — The staff email travels, and the codebase already decided it should not.

The row carries `email`. `identity.service.js:45-53` says why the assignee
picker does not: *"Email is deliberately absent — a picker does not need staff
addresses, and every field that travels is a field that has to keep being
safe."* A load report needs a name and a number for the same reason a picker
needs a name and an id. Drop `email` from the query, the response and the
OpenAPI entry.

### 4 — A ticket can fall out of both figures.

`agents` covers live staff; `unassigned` covers `assignee_id IS NULL`. A live,
non-terminal ticket assigned to a **disabled** account is in neither, and the
report is short by one with nothing saying so.

`IDENTITY-9-API (CRM-54)` hands those tickets back on disable, so it should not
arise — which is exactly what was said about the account projection that
reported every disabled row as live, and about the out-of-set status in
`queue-by-status`. Both times the check cost one test.

**Report a total of live non-terminal tickets and prove the parts add up to it**,
with a test that sets `users.deleted_at` directly on somebody holding work. If
the sum can drift, an admin should see the drift rather than a tidy report that
has quietly lost a ticket.

### 5 — This OpenAPI document has no schemas and no security. Third time.

`security`, `required`, `properties`, `type: integer` — the file has none of
that anywhere: no `components`, no `schema`, no `security`, no `parameters`.
One prose description per response, consistent across every story. The key
carries the `/api/v1` prefix.

### 6 — `requireAdmin` does not exist.

The plan extends the factory to `reportsRouter({ …, agentLoad, requireAdmin })`
and then hedges about it. `reports.routes.js:12` builds its own guard —
`const adminOnly = requirePermission((subject) => subject.role === 'admin')` —
and the file is cited at line 6 in the same plan. Use `adminOnly`; add no
parameter.

### 7 — The reader's shape does not match its two siblings.

`createAgentLoadReader` is written to return a bare function. Both existing
readers return `{ read(actor) }`, and the router calls
`queueByStatus.read(req.subject)`. Match them.

### And one the plan got right, plus one to tighten

Keep the `IN ()` guard it proposes — an empty role list would be a SQL error
rather than an empty answer.

`ORDER BY u.name COLLATE NOCASE` has no tiebreak, and the plan says to accept
that. Add `u.id`: two agents sharing a name would otherwise swap places between
two reads of the same data, which is the defect L-19 exists for and which cost
this repository an index comment to fix once already.

## Story Goal

Add an admin-only backend report that returns, in a single response:

1. A **row per live staff user** (users with `deleted_at IS NULL` whose role is in `STAFF_ROLES`), each carrying a `load` count of tickets still on the person — assigned to them and neither `resolved` nor `closed`. Idle staff appear with `load: 0`, not omitted.
2. A separate `unassigned` figure counting live, non-terminal tickets whose `assignee_id IS NULL`. Unassigned work is **not** folded into any agent row.

Out of scope for this story:

- The web screen (`REPORTS-3-WEB (CRM-129)`).
- Date-window filtering (`REPORTS-4-API (CRM-130)`).
- Any "capacity", target or ranking — this endpoint counts, it does not judge.
- Disabled accounts' historical work — `IDENTITY-9-API (CRM-54)` reassigns their tickets on disable; they simply do not appear here.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Repository query: staff rows with load, and the unassigned figure

**File:** `api/src/features/reports/reports.repository.js`

Add two exported functions alongside the existing three. Keep the same shape: plain `export function` taking `db`, using `.prepare(...).all()`, mapping to a small POJO array or number.

#### 1a — `countAssignedLoadByUser(db, { staffRoles, terminalStatuses })`

The rows come from `users`, with ticket counts joined on. **`GROUP BY tickets.assignee_id` is deliberately avoided** — that phrasing cannot return a person holding zero tickets, which is the whole point of the story.

```js
// Load per live staff user.
//
// The rows come from `users`, not from `tickets`: an admin opens this report
// to find the person holding nothing, and GROUP BY tickets.assignee_id can
// only return people who hold something. `LEFT JOIN` fills a zero for idle
// staff.
//
// "Live staff" means `users.deleted_at IS NULL` and role in STAFF_ROLES —
// a disabled account cannot take work, and a customer never holds a ticket.
//
// "Load" means work still on the person: assigned, not deleted, and not in a
// terminal status. The terminal pair is derived from STATUSES rather than
// spelled twice.
export function countAssignedLoadByUser(db, { staffRoles, terminalStatuses }) {
  const rolePlaceholders = staffRoles.map(() => '?').join(', ');
  const statusPlaceholders = terminalStatuses.map(() => '?').join(', ');
  return db
    .prepare(`
      SELECT u.id AS user_id, u.name AS name, u.email AS email, u.role AS role,
             COUNT(t.id) AS n
      FROM users u
      LEFT JOIN tickets t
        ON t.assignee_id = u.id
       AND t.deleted_at IS NULL
       AND t.status NOT IN (${statusPlaceholders})
      WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
        AND u.role IN (${rolePlaceholders})
      GROUP BY u.id
      ORDER BY u.name COLLATE NOCASE
    `)
    .all(...terminalStatuses, ...staffRoles)
    .map((row) => ({
      userId: row.user_id,
      name: row.name,
      email: row.email,
      role: row.role,
      load: row.n,
    }));
}
```

Confirm the exact user column names (`name`, `email`) against `0005__users.sql` before finalising the SELECT.

#### 1b — `countUnassignedLoad(db, { terminalStatuses })`

```js
// Unassigned live tickets that are not in a terminal status. Reported as its
// own figure, never folded into a "nobody" row.
export function countUnassignedLoad(db, { terminalStatuses }) {
  const statusPlaceholders = terminalStatuses.map(() => '?').join(', ');
  return db
    .prepare(`
      SELECT COUNT(*) AS n
      FROM tickets
      WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
        AND assignee_id IS NULL
        AND status NOT IN (${statusPlaceholders})
    `)
    .get(...terminalStatuses).n;
}
```

**Do not** import `STAFF_ROLES` or `STATUSES` inside this file. The repository is dumb: it takes the enum values as parameters. The reader passes them in.

```js
import { STAFF_ROLES } from '../identity/index.js';
import { STATUSES } from '../tickets/index.js';
import {
  countAssignedLoadByUser,
  countUnassignedLoad,
} from './reports.repository.js';

// Corrected — review item 2. There is nothing in STATUSES to derive this from,
// and a filter naming both members is two literals wearing a derivation.
const OFF_THE_PLATE = Object.freeze(['resolved', 'closed']);

export function createAgentLoadReader({ db }) {
  return function readAgentLoad() {
    const agents = countAssignedLoadByUser(db, {
      staffRoles: STAFF_ROLES,
      terminalStatuses: TERMINAL_STATUSES,
    });
    const unassigned = countUnassignedLoad(db, {
      terminalStatuses: TERMINAL_STATUSES,
    });
    return { agents, unassigned };
  };
}
```

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Zero staff exist** — response is `{ agents: [], unassigned: N }`. The `LEFT JOIN` shape naturally produces no rows; the unassigned count is independent.
- **Staff user with no tickets ever** — appears with `load: 0` (this is the story). Enforced by `LEFT JOIN users → tickets` in `countAssignedLoadByUser`.
- **Staff user whose only tickets are `resolved` or `closed`** — `load: 0`. Enforced by `t.status NOT IN (?, ?)` in the join predicate (not the WHERE, so the user still appears).
- **Disabled staff (`deleted_at IS NOT NULL`)** — no row. Enforced by `WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL`. Aligns with `IDENTITY-9-API (CRM-54)` which reassigns their tickets on disable.
- **Customer role** — never appears. Enforced by `u.role IN (?, ?, …)` bound to `STAFF_ROLES`.
- **Unassigned tickets** — never attributed to an agent row; reported only in the top-level `unassigned` field. Enforced by `assignee_id = u.id` in the join (a NULL `assignee_id` does not match any user).
- **Soft-deleted tickets** — excluded from both counts (`t.deleted_at IS NULL` on the join; `deleted_at IS NULL` in the unassigned query).
- **Non-admin caller** — 403 from the admin middleware **before** the reader runs. Enforced in `reports.routes.js` and covered by `staff-only.guarantee.test.js`.
- **Missing session / anonymous** — 401 from the upstream auth middleware, decided before the admin check.
- **Ties on name** — `ORDER BY u.name COLLATE NOCASE, u.id` (review item 7's companion). Without the tiebreak two agents sharing a name swap places between two reads of the same data, which is L-19.
- **Empty `STAFF_ROLES` or `TERMINAL_STATUSES`** — impossible in current code, but the placeholder-building would produce `IN ()` which is a SQL error. Add a defensive `if (!staffRoles.length) return []` and analogous guard for terminal statuses in the reader.

## Done Criteria

- [x] Every live staff member has a row, and the ones holding nothing say `load: 0` — the rows come from `users` with the counts joined on, so the person an admin opened the report to find is in it.
- [x] Load means work still on the person: assigned, not soft-deleted, and neither resolved nor closed. The status filter is in the JOIN and not the WHERE — in the WHERE it would drop the agent along with their finished tickets, so somebody who cleared their queue would vanish for having done the work.
- [x] A disabled account has no row; a customer never appears.
- [x] Unassigned work is its own figure and never a row among the people.
- [x] **The parts are checkable against the whole.** `open` counts every live non-terminal ticket and `unaccounted` is what the rows and the unassigned figure do not reach. A test disables an account straight through the column — so the ticket is not handed back the way `IDENTITY-9-API (CRM-54)` hands it back — and the report says `unaccounted: 1` instead of quietly being short.
- [x] No row carries an email. `identity.service.js:45-53` says why the assignee picker omits it, and a load report needs a name and a number for the same reason.
- [x] `OFF_THE_PLATE` is written out with its reason, not filtered out of `STATUSES` (review item 2). `TRANSITIONS` makes `closed` the only terminal status, so "terminal" was the wrong word, and a filter naming both members is two literals wearing a derivation.
- [x] `STAFF_ROLES` reached through `identity/index.js`, added there in this story; `verify-architecture` passes.
- [x] Ordered by name with `u.id` as the tiebreak, so two agents sharing a name do not swap between reads (L-19).
- [x] Admin-only via middleware; an agent gets 403 before the reader runs. **No census file was touched** (review item 1).
- [x] Documented in `api/openapi.json`, prose like the rest of the file.
- [x] `cd api && npm test` — 606 pass, 0 fail.
- [x] No AI-attribution strings in the diff.

## What the mutation pass proved

| # | what was broken | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | an inner join, so idle agents vanish | 2 fail |
| A2 | the status filter moves to the WHERE | 6 fail |
| A3 | disabled accounts get rows | 2 fail |
| A4 | the unaccounted gap is swallowed | 1 fail |
| A5 | the address travels after all | 1 fail |

A2 is the one worth keeping. Moving `t.status NOT IN (…)` from the JOIN to the
WHERE looks like tidying and is the same defect as the inner join wearing
different clothes: an agent whose every ticket is finished disappears from the
report for having finished them.

## What this story changed about the loop

The review caught the census instruction for the **second consecutive plan**,
with `L-68` already written and sitting in the file the intake tells the
planner to read first. A hint that fails twice is not a mechanism (L-54), so
`verify-plan.mjs` now fails a plan that puts a route into a census's list and
claims that proves the guarantee.

It took three passes to scope. The first draft failed ten shipped plans doing
legitimate things — writing a new census, extending what one asserts, adding a
genuinely defensible exemption row — and a check that cries wolf gets relaxed
until it catches nothing. The defect is the **claim**, not the edit. Four probes
in `verify-plan.selftest.mjs` hold it there: one that must fire, and three
near-misses that must stay silent.

It also caught a leftover in this very plan that the hand review had missed —
a verification step still saying "the updated `staff-only.guarantee.test.js`
still passes".
